title: Evercore Sees Alphabet TPU Sales Reaching $75 Billion in 2027
excerpt: Evercore ISI kept a $450 target on Alphabet and lifted its 2027 Google Cloud forecast to $213 billion, while J.P. Morgan raised its target to $425 on expectations cloud revenue will double in the third quarter.
body:
• Evercore ISI reiterated an Outperform rating and a $450 price target on Alphabet — about 30% upside from the last close — forecasting external TPU hardware sales of $7.5 billion in the second half of 2026, $75 billion in 2027 and $113 billion in 2028.
  • Evercore raised its 2027 Google Cloud revenue estimate to $213 billion from $180 billion, with TPUs alone accounting for about 35% of cloud revenue that year, and lifted its 2027 Alphabet revenue forecast to $651 billion from $618 billion.
  • J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth separately raised his Alphabet target to $425 from $420, implying about 22% upside, and now expects Google Cloud revenue to grow 100% in the third quarter.
  • Alphabet reports third-quarter earnings on Oct. 28 — the first hard test of whether contracted TPU demand is converting into recognised revenue at the pace analysts now model.

Alphabet's custom AI chips, built for its own data centres, are emerging as a standalone hardware business large enough to move the company's forecasts. Evercore ISI reiterated its Outperform rating and $450 price target on Alphabet this week, arguing that external sales of Google's Tensor Processing Units could generate $75 billion in revenue in 2027 and $113 billion in 2028, according to Seeking Alpha's summary of the note.

The call lands days before Alphabet reports third-quarter earnings on Oct. 28. The question is no longer only how fast Google Cloud can rent AI capacity — it is how much revenue Google can book by selling the underlying silicon itself, directly into customers' own data centres.

The TPU Thesis: From Internal Advantage to External Business

Google originally developed TPU systems for its own cloud workloads. It is now selling them to outside customers, including AI model maker Anthropic and Meta Platforms, Investor's Business Daily reported. Evercore estimates TPU hardware sales of about $7.5 billion in the second half of 2026. Alphabet began recognising revenue from TPU-system sales in the second quarter, and expects the significant majority of revenue from existing agreements to be recognised in 2027.

https://x.com/SeekingAlpha/status/2111213105950994462

Evercore describes three monetisation routes: renting TPU processing through Google Cloud, selling complete systems for a customer's own data centre, and selling TPUs through a Blackstone joint venture. Broadcom is Alphabet's manufacturing partner, and Evercore assumes a 30% gross margin and 15% to 20% operating margin across 2026 to 2028.

"TPUs are evolving from an internal technology advantage into an external hardware business."

— Evercore ISI, in its Alphabet note

Industry checks cited by Evercore found TPUs could offer 20% to 40% lower costs for customers with experienced engineering teams. That cost edge is the core of the pitch against Nvidia, whose general-purpose GPUs dominate AI training and inference but carry premium pricing and tight supply.

What the Analysts Changed

The estimate revisions are large. Evercore raised its 2027 Google Cloud revenue estimate to $213 billion from $180 billion — a near-doubling of the business in a single year on its model, with growth of another 40% to $298 billion in 2028. Even excluding TPUs, Evercore expects cloud revenue to grow 39% in 2027 and 35% in 2028. Its overall Alphabet revenue forecast for 2027 rose to $651 billion from $618 billion, and the $450 target is based on 25 times its 2028 GAAP earnings estimate and 14 times its 2028 EBITDA estimate.

J.P. Morgan moved in the same direction, on a tighter timeline. Analyst Doug Anmuth raised his price target to $425 from $420, implying the stock can rally about 22% from Wednesday's closing price of $347.64, Barron's reported. Anmuth now expects Google Cloud revenue to grow 100% in the third quarter, up from a recent 88% forecast, and raised his 2027 earnings forecast by 3% to $14.05 a share.

"The primary driver of the increase is greater TPU sale inclusion, and we could still be conservative."

— Doug Anmuth, J.P. Morgan analyst

The starting point is strong. Google reported second-quarter cloud revenue of $24.77 billion, up 82% year over year and ahead of $22.46 billion estimates. Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai has said the company will deliver TPUs to a select group of customers in their own data centres as demand grows from AI labs and high-performance computing users, The Motley Fool noted.

What It Means for Google Cloud — and for Nvidia

If Evercore is right, TPUs would account for roughly 35% of Google Cloud revenue in 2027. That makes Google a merchant chip supplier as well as a cloud operator, and creates a direct, if partial, challenge to Nvidia: TPUs are less flexible than GPUs, but for large, standardised AI jobs their cost advantage is material.

The barriers are real. Evercore flagged software limitations, a shortage of specialised talent and platform performance gaps that could slow adoption beyond sophisticated buyers such as Anthropic and Meta, plus regulatory scrutiny and competition from Amazon and Microsoft's Azure. Hardware is also lower-margin than cloud services, so a TPU-heavy mix would lift revenue faster than profit.

Investors are withholding judgment. Alphabet shares traded about 3% lower on Friday amid broader pressure on large technology stocks. Its Oct. 28 results — for a company valued at about $4.23 trillion, the world's third-largest — will show whether third-quarter cloud growth and early TPU recognition support the higher base case analysts have just built.
